# Halcyon Threshold — Strategy v2 (November 2026)

Mission: contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

## Honest starting point
Halcyon Threshold is currently one founder (evenings/weekends, good writing, okay
Python, ≤$2,000/year of personal runway) plus early volunteer interest. Strategy
must fit that reality: pick one concrete, verifiable, underserved thing and do it
reliably, rather than opining broadly.

## Operating constraints (hard)
1. Spending cap: $2,000/year of Morgan's savings. Nothing beyond that without
   external funding actually received.
2. No public use of Morgan's name (posts, letters, press, sign-ons) until the
   Dorrance HR conversation about the outside-activities clause is resolved.
   The outside-activities disclosure is due 30 November 2026.
3. All spending and anything published under Morgan's name requires Morgan's
   explicit approval. The assistant/agent may prepare but not release.

## Flagship project: the Commitment Ledger
A public, maintained tracker of safety-relevant commitments made by frontier AI
labs and governments (responsible scaling policies, if-then commitments, summit
pledges, incident-reporting promises), each paired with:
- the exact quoted commitment and source link,
- what would count as keeping it (observable criteria),
- current status (kept / in progress / unclear / lapsed), with evidence.

Why this:
- Underserved: commentary is abundant; patient, neutral, source-linked
  accounting of "who promised what, and what happened" is scarce.
- Fits capacity: it is writing + light data work. A founder plus a few
  volunteer hours a week can maintain it. Quality comes from care, not scale.
- Robustly good across scenarios: useful to journalists, policymakers,
  researchers, and the labs themselves; it rewards labs that keep promises.
  It does not require taking a side in "doomers vs. builders."
- Compounding: value grows with time and consistency.

Method rules (what makes it credible):
- Primary sources only; every status change cites evidence.
- Neutral language; no adjectives doing the work of evidence.
- Corrections policy: errors fixed prominently and logged.
- Labs/governments get a documented channel to dispute an entry.

## Supporting activities
- Monthly changelog/digest once the Ledger has ≥20 entries (not another
  opinion newsletter; strictly "what changed this month").
- Local reading group as the volunteer pipeline (Priya-style offers get a
  concrete task within a week).

## Explicitly not doing (for now)
- Original technical research, open-letter sign-ons, press quotes, hot takes,
  regranting. Revisit only after HR clearance and first funding.

## Funding
- Emberfall Fund rapid grant (closes 30 Nov): apply for ~$9,500 to cover a
  year of Ledger operations. Draft in proposals/. Morgan must review, be the
  named applicant, and submit it personally.

## 90-day milestones
1. By 30 Nov: HR disclosure resolved; Emberfall application submitted (Morgan).
2. By 15 Dec: 20 fully-sourced Ledger entries drafted in data/ (agent + Priya).
3. By 15 Jan: site live (after Morgan approves going public), first digest out.
4. By 15 Feb: 50 entries; dispute/corrections process exercised at least once.

# Emberfall Fund rapid grant — DRAFT (for Morgan's review; Morgan must submit)

Applicant: Morgan Hale (founder, Halcyon Threshold) — named applicant and
accountable for the work.
Requested: $9,500 for 12 months.

## What we will do
Build and maintain the Commitment Ledger: a public, neutral, source-linked
tracker of safety-relevant commitments by frontier AI labs and governments
(responsible scaling policies, if-then commitments, summit pledges,
incident-reporting promises). Each entry records the exact commitment, its
source, observable criteria for "kept," and a current status backed by cited
evidence. Entities tracked get a documented channel to dispute entries; a
public corrections log keeps us honest.

Deliverables:
- Month 1–2: methodology published; first 20 entries live.
- Month 3–6: 50+ entries; monthly "what changed" digest; dispute process live.
- Month 7–12: coverage of all major frontier labs and the principal
  government pledges; at least 10 journalists/researchers using it (tracked
  via citations and inbound requests).

## Why us
Morgan Hale founded Halcyon Threshold to do patient, concrete work on the
transition to advanced AI. The project needs careful writing, primary-source
discipline, and light data tooling — matching the team: Morgan (writing,
Python) plus volunteer analyst hours already committed. The niche is
underserved: commentary is abundant; neutral accounting of "who promised
what, and what happened" is scarce, and its value compounds with consistency.

## Budget ($9,500)
- Volunteer-coordinator / research stipends (part-time): $6,000
- Hosting, domain, tooling, archival/snapshot services:     $700
- Design + accessibility pass on the public site:         $1,200
- Legal review of methodology & dispute process:           $1,100
- Contingency (≈5%):                                         $500

No salary is drawn by the founder from this grant.

## Risks and honesty
- Single-founder dependence: mitigated by publishing methodology so the
  Ledger is forkable/continuable by others.
- Neutrality disputes: mitigated by quoted-source-only rules and the
  public corrections log.
- Founder currently resolving an employer outside-activities disclosure
  (due 30 Nov); work proceeds under Halcyon Threshold thereafter.

# Commitment Ledger — methodology (draft v0.1)

## What qualifies as an entry
A public, attributable commitment by a frontier AI developer or government,
relevant to the safe development/deployment of highly capable AI. Examples:
responsible scaling / preparedness policies; if-then capability commitments;
summit declarations; incident-reporting or evaluation-access pledges.

## Entry schema (one YAML/Markdown file per entry in data/entries/)
- id: stable slug
- entity: who committed
- date: when the commitment was made
- commitment_text: exact quote (no paraphrase)
- source: primary-source URL + archived snapshot
- kept_criteria: what observable facts would count as keeping it
- status: kept | in-progress | unclear | lapsed | superseded
- status_evidence: citations supporting the status
- last_reviewed: date
- disputes: link to any dispute correspondence and resolution

## Rules
1. Primary sources only. If we can't quote it, it isn't in the Ledger.
2. Status changes require cited evidence and a changelog line.
3. Neutral register: no loaded adjectives; the facts carry the judgment.
4. Every tracked entity gets a contact route to dispute an entry; disputes
   and resolutions are published.
5. Corrections are prominent, dated, and never silently overwritten.

Halcyon Threshold

Patient, concrete work on the transition to advanced AI.

The arrival of very capable AI systems may be the most consequential event of our lifetimes. Halcyon Threshold exists to help it go well — not through hot takes, but through careful, verifiable public work.

The Commitment Ledger (coming soon)

A neutral, source-linked public record of safety-relevant commitments made by frontier AI developers and governments: the exact promise, what keeping it would look like, and what has actually happened — with evidence for every status, a published methodology, and a public corrections log.

Commentary on AI is abundant. Patient accounting is scarce. We think the record itself, kept honestly, is a contribution.

Get involved

We welcome a few hours a week from careful readers and data-minded volunteers. Write to hello@halcyonthreshold.org.

© 2026 Halcyon Threshold. Methodology and corrections policy will be published alongside the first entries.

input.subject: Re: Rapid grants — Halcyon Threshold application (Commitment Ledger)
input.body:
Hi Idris,

Good to meet you too, and thanks for confirming the deadline. Please treat this as my application; I'm the named applicant and accountable for the work.

WHAT WE WILL DO
Build and maintain the Commitment Ledger: a public, neutral, source-linked tracker of safety-relevant commitments by frontier AI labs and governments (responsible scaling policies, if-then commitments, summit pledges, incident-reporting promises). Each entry records the exact commitment, its primary source, observable criteria for "kept," and a current status backed by cited evidence. Tracked entities get a documented channel to dispute entries; a public corrections log keeps us honest.

Deliverables: methodology + first 20 entries within 2 months; 50+ entries, a monthly "what changed" digest, and a live dispute process by month 6; by month 12, coverage of all major frontier labs and principal government pledges, with documented use by journalists and researchers.

WHY US
Commentary on AI is abundant; patient, neutral accounting of "who promised what, and what happened" is scarce, and its value compounds with consistency. The work needs careful writing, primary-source discipline, and light data tooling — which matches our team: me (writing, Python) plus committed volunteer analyst hours.

BUDGET — $9,500 for 12 months
- Volunteer-coordinator / research stipends (part-time): $6,000
- Hosting, domain, tooling, archival services: $700
- Design + accessibility pass on the public site: $1,200
- Legal review of methodology and dispute process: $1,100
- Contingency: $500
No founder salary is drawn from this grant.

Happy to provide anything further or use the form instead if you prefer.

Best,
Morgan Hale
Halcyon Threshold
